# The Windows App SDK pin (architecture sections 13.2 and 14).
#
# ONE FILE, THREE READERS. tools/fetch-winappsdk.ps1 downloads and verifies from
# it, src/app/winappsdk.cmake locates the unpacked packages from it, and
# tools/scan-licenses.ps1 checks the licence of every line in it. They used to be
# three copies of the same five version numbers, and the failure mode of that is
# a build that links one release of the SDK against the metadata of another --
# which does not fail at the link, it fails at run time with a type that does not
# activate.
#
# Format, one package per line, pipe-separated, no spaces around the bars:
#
#     id | version | sha256-of-the-nupkg | licence | licence file in the package
#
# THE CHECKSUM IS OVER THE .nupkg, not over anything unpacked. A .nupkg is a zip
# and unpacking is not reproducible byte for byte, so the archive is the only
# thing there is a stable hash of. Each one below was taken from a package NuGet
# had already validated against the feed's own SHA-512, so the chain is: the
# feed's hash, checked by NuGet at install; this hash, checked by us at fetch.
#
# TO UPDATE: change the version, run the fetcher, and let it fail -- it prints
# the hash it got. Put that hash here only once you know why the old one stopped
# matching. The three WindowsAppSDK sub-packages version independently but ship
# as one release, and MORPH_WINAPPSDK_MAJORMINOR in winappsdk.cmake has to be the
# major.minor of that release: headers, metadata and the framework package the
# process resolves at run time must all be one release of one product.
#
# LICENCES. Section 14's allowlist is about copyleft risk in code that is LINKED
# into Morph. Three of these are not on it and cannot be: the Windows App SDK is
# a Microsoft first-party redistributable under the Microsoft Software License
# Terms, which is proprietary and grants redistribution as part of an
# application. That is a deliberate exception with a reason, not an omission --
# scan-licenses.ps1 states it in the report rather than passing them silently,
# because the whole point of A2 was that the gate had a blind spot here.
